description:
Ubicación:

Guadalajara, Jalisco, México.

Descripción de la compañía.

Ferrero es una empresa familiar con una perspectiva verdaderamente mundial y progresista y marcas icónicas como Nutella®, Tic Tac®, Ferrero Rocher®, Raffaello®, Kinder Bueno® y Kinder Sorpresa®. El amor por nuestras marcas sigue creciendo al igual que lo hace nuestro alcance internacional. Representada en más de 50 países y con productos vendidos en más de 170, el Grupo Ferrero encanta a numerosas generaciones en todo el planeta. ¿Cuál es el secreto de nuestro éxito mundial? 40,000 empleados especializados que celebran tanto el cuidado como la calidad para forjar un negocio, carreras profesionales y marcas de las que nos sentimos orgullosos. Únete a nosotros, podrías ser uno de ellos.

Acerca del Rol:

Nos encontramos en búsqueda de una persona responsable, comprometida, con ganas de aprender y desarrollarse en el área de Marketing. Si tienes un perfil analítico, te gusta generar insights y colaborar con equipos multidisciplinarios para la creación de estrategias de Marcas ¡esta oportunidad puede ser interesante para ti!

Postúlate y podrás formar parte del equipo que hace de Ferrero un lugar extraordinario para trabajar.

Principales Responsabilidades:


Serás responsable de actualizar y realizar reportes. 
Darás seguimiento de tareas y pendientes del equipo. 
Serás responsable de participar en análisis de información de mercado y desempeño. 
Brindarás soporte en la descarga, actualización y seguimiento de información Nielsen u otras plataformas de interpretación de data. 
Darás soporte operativo para presentaciones y documentos internos.


Acerca de ti:


Estudiantes activos de Lic. En Marketing, Administración, Negocios, Ingeniería Industrial o afines (Garantizar estatus activo de al menos un año).
Disponibilidad para laborar 6 hrs diarias de lunes a viernes en horario matutino.
Inglés Avanzado Conversacional (Competencia profesional oral y escrito).
Paquetería Office: Excel nivel intermedio.
Perfil proactivo, analítico (lógico-numérico), comunicación efectiva, organización, estructurado, atención al detalle y con enfoque a los resultados.
Interés por aprender y desarrollarse en el área, en un entorno dinámico.


Nuestros Beneficios y ventajas:

Carreras con cuidado integrado: descubre nuestros beneficios aquí.

Acerca de Ferrero:

Ferrero comenzó su trayectoria en la pequeña ciudad de Alba en Piamonte, Italia, en 1946. Hoy en día, es una de las empresas de alimentos dulces envasados más grandes del mundo, con muchas marcas icónicas que se venden en todo el mundo. Descubre más sobre Ferrero en ferrero.com.

¿Cómo ser exitoso en el rol y en Ferrero?

Consumidores, calidad y servicio son la clave de todo cuanto hacemos. Así pues, para cosechar el éxito en Ferrero, deberás orientarte al consumidor y al producto tanto como nosotros: dedicarte a lograr buenos resultados para los clientes en todo el mundo.

DE&I en Ferrero:

Ferrero se compromete a construir una cultura diversa e inclusiva donde todos los empleados se sientan bienvenidos, valorados y tengan las mismas oportunidades. Creemos que todos nuestros empleados tienen el mismo talento, cada uno a su manera. Al fomentar la curiosidad y las habilidades naturales de nuestros empleados, les proporcionamos, generación tras generación, los medios para alcanzar el éxito personal y profesional, permitiéndoles forjar su trayectoria en Ferrero. La diversidad de nuestros talentos es lo que hace que nuestro entorno laboral sea multicultural, innovador y altamente gratificante. Descubre más aquí.

description:
Descripción de la empresa Talento mx360 es una empresa enfocada en conectar talento con oportunidades en diferentes sectores, con especial atención en perfiles de marketing y ventas. Trabajamos en colaboración con diversas organizaciones para apoyar sus procesos de selección y desarrollo profesional. Nos orientamos a crear experiencias laborales de calidad, donde las personas puedan crecer y aportar valor real. Fomentamos un entorno inclusivo, dinámico y orientado a resultados, ideal para quienes quieren impulsar su carrera en marketing.

Descripción del puesto Como Asistente de marketing, apoyarás en la ejecución de campañas y acciones de marketing, tanto online como offline, asegurando que se cumplan los objetivos establecidos. En tu día a día te encargarás de preparar materiales de comunicación, gestionar publicaciones en redes sociales, apoyar en el seguimiento de leads y coordinar con el equipo de ventas para alinear las acciones comerciales. También colaborarás en la organización de eventos y activaciones, así como en la recopilación y análisis de información de mercado y de la competencia. Este es un puesto de tiempo completo, presencial y se desarrolla en México.

Requisitos

 

Aptitudes en comunicación, redacción y manejo de redes sociales, con capacidad para adaptar mensajes a diferentes públicos.
Aptitudes en investigación de mercado y análisis básico de datos para apoyar decisiones de marketing.
Aptitudes en atención al cliente y servicio postventa, con enfoque en la satisfacción y fidelización de personas usuarias.
Aptitudes en ventas y sales & marketing, apoyando la generación y seguimiento de oportunidades comerciales.
Formación en marketing, comunicación, administración o áreas afines; se valora experiencia previa en puestos de apoyo de marketing.
Manejo de herramientas ofimáticas (Excel, PowerPoint) y plataformas digitales de marketing; se valoran conocimientos en CRM y email marketing.

title: PPC Marketing Specialist (Remote)
skills: Own a set of DTC accounts as the strategist, the buyer, and the client's direct point of contact. Budgets run from $5k/mo to well into six figures a month
Own the client relationship. There is no account manager between you and them. You present the results, the plan, and the reasoning, and you are the one who answers when something is not working

Audit before you touch anything. Every account we take over gets a real review first: campaign and ad group structure, keywords versus search terms, negatives, bidding strategy per campaign type, impression share, feed health, landing pages, audiences, and conversion tracking. Then a Loom walking the client through what you found. That Loom is how we sell and it is how we keep people

Run brand and non brand as different businesses. Brand is mostly assisted conversion and it usually belongs on target impression share, not target CPA. Non brand is where the growth is and where the waste is. Report them separately or you are reporting nothing

Know what PMax is actually doing. The most common mistake we see is optimizing PMax against an incremental CAC when half the volume inside it is branded. If you cannot separate those two, you cannot set a target
Keep Google's automation on a leash. Auto applied recommendations, auto applied assets, and auto created sitelinks have cost our clients real money. We audit for them on a schedule
Own the feed. Merchant Center hygiene, product titles, disapprovals, promotions, and what the feed does to Shopping and PMax delivery

Own the tracking. GA4, GTM, Shopify goal imports versus a raw Google Ads tag, enhanced conversions, offline conversion imports for the lead gen accounts. When the numbers do not reconcile, you are the one who finds out why
Diagnose the bottleneck, then go fix it. Creative, offer, AOV, landing page, checkout, tracking. Nobody is going to reassign it to another team
Build the things the account needs. Landing pages, scripts, reporting, whatever removes the constraint. We are heavy AI users and we expect you to build, not just prompt

You have done this with real money. Hands on Google Ads at meaningful spend on DTC and eCommerce, with results you can walk us through: CPA, ROAS, revenue, and what you actually changed to get them. Shopping and PMax specifically, not just search
You are fluent in the whole stack, not one campaign type. Search, Shopping, PMax, Demand Gen, YouTube, Merchant Center, GA4, GTM. Bing is a nice to have

You are AI native, and you build. This is a requirement, not a bonus. You should already be using Claude or equivalent as a working tool rather than a novelty, and you should be able to build and ship a landing page with it

You can communicate your ideas in English at a native or near native level. You will be in front of clients constantly. You need to explain your thinking clearly, sell an idea on its merits, push back when a client is about to force the account into mediocrity, and raise a problem before it becomes a fire. This matters as much as anything else on this list
You are skeptical of your own numbers. You would rather run the holdout than protect the dashboard
You can work US Eastern business hours for client calls. Where you live is up to you
Bonus: you have built or operated your own Shopify store, or you have run Meta at spend too
"That was not my role" is in your vocabulary. It is the fastest way to end an interview here. If the feed was the problem on an account you ran, you should have done something about the feed
You want to be told what to do this week
You need a ticketing system to know what matters
You quote blended ROAS as if it settles the question
description:
Everyone can run a search campaign. Almost nobody can tell you whether it worked.

That is the whole job.

Google will happily show you a 6x ROAS built almost entirely out of people who already knew your client's name. It will auto apply assets you did not ask for. It will report a number that makes a client feel great and tells you nothing about whether you grew the business.

So we do not hire people to manage Google Ads. We hire marketers who can tell the difference between demand they created and demand they harvested, and who can prove it to a client's face.

At Sweat Pants Agency we work with around 50 DTC and eCommerce brands, 20 to 25 of them on paid media. We spend $6 to $9M a month on Meta and $1 to $2M a month on Google. We are the only agency behind two INC #1 fastest growing brands, both from zero.

You would own a set of our Google accounts end to end.

Here is what "end to end" actually means.

You are the account manager. We do not have any. You talk to the client directly. You write the updates, you run the calls, and you defend the call you made. The reason we do it this way is ownership. When you are the person answering for the account, it is your result, not somebody else's summary of your result.

You own the whole funnel, not the campaign. Feed and Merchant Center, search and Shopping and PMax, Demand Gen and YouTube, the landing page, and the conversion tracking underneath all of it. If the feed is why Shopping is starving, that is yours. If the page is why the clicks do not convert, that is yours too. Our team ships advertorials, comparison pages, and PDPs in Claude Code, deploys them to Vercel, points a subdomain at them, and tests them live before anything touches the client's Shopify theme.

You are expected to have an opinion about attribution and to defend it. We optimize to NC-CPA and NC-ROAS, not blended and not last click. We have turned brand search off to see what actually shifts to organic. We run geo holdouts. If a campaign is not incremental, we would rather know than keep the number.

You can live anywhere. We are remote and we hire worldwide. The one hard requirement is that you can take client calls during US Eastern business hours, because you are the client's point of contact. The rest of your day is yours. Nobody here is on a time clock. We judge you on output.

If you want a lane, a ticket queue, and a scope document, this is a bad fit and we will both know it fast.

If you want to own the whole picture and be judged on whether the number moved, keep reading.

Build the things the account needs. Landing pages, scripts, reporting, whatever removes the constraint. We are heavy AI users and we expect you to build, not just prompt

"That was not my role" is in your vocabulary. It is the fastest way to end an interview here. If the feed was the problem on an account you ran, you should have done something about the feed
You want to be told what to do this week
You need a ticketing system to know what matters
You quote blended ROAS as if it settles the question


Benefits

Why this role is exciting

This is not a maintenance job. You would have real influence over how we run Google across the agency.

You will work on real brands with real budgets. We test aggressively. We learn quickly. We build frameworks that scale.

You get trust on day one. You get a lot of autonomy. Some people thrive with it. You will get feedback fast either way, and if you make it through the first 30 days you will probably be here for a long time. Our retention on this team is very good and that is not an accident.

You will grow into senior strategy. We want people who want more responsibility. If you perform, you will grow.

Own the client relationship. There is no account manager between you and them. You present the results, the plan, and the reasoning, and you are the one who answers when something is not working

Audit before you touch anything. Every account we take over gets a real review first: campaign and ad group structure, keywords versus search terms, negatives, bidding strategy per campaign type, impression share, feed health, landing pages, audiences, and conversion tracking. Run brand and non brand as different businesses. Brand is mostly assisted conversion and it usually belongs on target impression share, not target CPA. Non brand is where the growth is and where the waste is. Report them separately or you are reporting nothing

Build the things the account needs. Landing pages, scripts, reporting, whatever removes the constraint. We are heavy AI users and we expect you to build, not just prompt

You have done this with real money. Hands on Google Ads at meaningful spend on DTC and eCommerce, with results you can walk us through: CPA, ROAS, revenue, and what you actually changed to get them. Shopping and PMax specifically, not just search

You are AI native, and you build. This is a requirement, not a bonus. You should already be using Claude or equivalent as a working tool rather than a novelty, and you should be able to build and ship a landing page with it

description:
Everyone can run a search campaign. Almost nobody can tell you whether it worked.

That is the whole job.

Google will happily show you a 6x ROAS built almost entirely out of people who already knew your client's name. It will auto apply assets you did not ask for. It will report a number that makes a client feel great and tells you nothing about whether you grew the business.

So we do not hire people to manage Google Ads. We hire marketers who can tell the difference between demand they created and demand they harvested, and who can prove it to a client's face.

At Sweat Pants Agency we work with around 50 DTC and eCommerce brands, 20 to 25 of them on paid media. We spend $6 to $9M a month on Meta and $1 to $2M a month on Google. We are the only agency behind two INC #1 fastest growing brands, both from zero.

You would own a set of our Google accounts end to end.

Here is what "end to end" actually means.

You are the account manager. We do not have any. You talk to the client directly. You write the updates, you run the calls, and you defend the call you made. The reason we do it this way is ownership. When you are the person answering for the account, it is your result, not somebody else's summary of your result.

You own the whole funnel, not the campaign. Feed and Merchant Center, search and Shopping and PMax, Demand Gen and YouTube, the landing page, and the conversion tracking underneath all of it. If the feed is why Shopping is starving, that is yours. If the page is why the clicks do not convert, that is yours too. Our team ships advertorials, comparison pages, and PDPs in Claude Code, deploys them to Vercel, points a subdomain at them, and tests them live before anything touches the client's Shopify theme.

You are expected to have an opinion about attribution and to defend it. We optimize to NC-CPA and NC-ROAS, not blended and not last click. We have turned brand search off to see what actually shifts to organic. We run geo holdouts. If a campaign is not incremental, we would rather know than keep the number.

You can live anywhere. We are remote and we hire worldwide. The one hard requirement is that you can take client calls during US Eastern business hours, because you are the client's point of contact. The rest of your day is yours. Nobody here is on a time clock. We judge you on output.

title: PPC Marketing Specialist (Remote)
skills: Own a set of DTC accounts as the strategist, the buyer, and the client's direct point of contact. Budgets run from $5k/mo to well into six figures a month
Own the client relationship. There is no account manager between you and them. You present the results, the plan, and the reasoning, and you are the one who answers when something is not working

Audit before you touch anything. Every account we take over gets a real review first: campaign and ad group structure, keywords versus search terms, negatives, bidding strategy per campaign type, impression share, feed health, landing pages, audiences, and conversion tracking. Then a Loom walking the client through what you found. That Loom is how we sell and it is how we keep people

Run brand and non brand as different businesses. Brand is mostly assisted conversion and it usually belongs on target impression share, not target CPA. Non brand is where the growth is and where the waste is. Report them separately or you are reporting nothing

Know what PMax is actually doing. The most common mistake we see is optimizing PMax against an incremental CAC when half the volume inside it is branded. If you cannot separate those two, you cannot set a target
Keep Google's automation on a leash. Auto applied recommendations, auto applied assets, and auto created sitelinks have cost our clients real money. We audit for them on a schedule
Own the feed. Merchant Center hygiene, product titles, disapprovals, promotions, and what the feed does to Shopping and PMax delivery

Own the tracking. GA4, GTM, Shopify goal imports versus a raw Google Ads tag, enhanced conversions, offline conversion imports for the lead gen accounts. When the numbers do not reconcile, you are the one who finds out why
Diagnose the bottleneck, then go fix it. Creative, offer, AOV, landing page, checkout, tracking. Nobody is going to reassign it to another team
Build the things the account needs. Landing pages, scripts, reporting, whatever removes the constraint. We are heavy AI users and we expect you to build, not just prompt

You have done this with real money. Hands on Google Ads at meaningful spend on DTC and eCommerce, with results you can walk us through: CPA, ROAS, revenue, and what you actually changed to get them. Shopping and PMax specifically, not just search
You are fluent in the whole stack, not one campaign type. Search, Shopping, PMax, Demand Gen, YouTube, Merchant Center, GA4, GTM. Bing is a nice to have

You are AI native, and you build. This is a requirement, not a bonus. You should already be using Claude or equivalent as a working tool rather than a novelty, and you should be able to build and ship a landing page with it

You can communicate your ideas in English at a native or near native level. You will be in front of clients constantly. You need to explain your thinking clearly, sell an idea on its merits, push back when a client is about to force the account into mediocrity, and raise a problem before it becomes a fire. This matters as much as anything else on this list
You are skeptical of your own numbers. You would rather run the holdout than protect the dashboard
You can work US Eastern business hours for client calls. Where you live is up to you
Bonus: you have built or operated your own Shopify store, or you have run Meta at spend too
"That was not my role" is in your vocabulary. It is the fastest way to end an interview here. If the feed was the problem on an account you ran, you should have done something about the feed
You want to be told what to do this week
You need a ticketing system to know what matters
You quote blended ROAS as if it settles the question
description:
Everyone can run a search campaign. Almost nobody can tell you whether it worked.

That is the whole job.

Google will happily show you a 6x ROAS built almost entirely out of people who already knew your client's name. It will auto apply assets you did not ask for. It will report a number that makes a client feel great and tells you nothing about whether you grew the business.

So we do not hire people to manage Google Ads. We hire marketers who can tell the difference between demand they created and demand they harvested, and who can prove it to a client's face.

At Sweat Pants Agency we work with around 50 DTC and eCommerce brands, 20 to 25 of them on paid media. We spend $6 to $9M a month on Meta and $1 to $2M a month on Google. We are the only agency behind two INC #1 fastest growing brands, both from zero.

You would own a set of our Google accounts end to end.

Here is what "end to end" actually means.

You are the account manager. We do not have any. You talk to the client directly. You write the updates, you run the calls, and you defend the call you made. The reason we do it this way is ownership. When you are the person answering for the account, it is your result, not somebody else's summary of your result.

You own the whole funnel, not the campaign. Feed and Merchant Center, search and Shopping and PMax, Demand Gen and YouTube, the landing page, and the conversion tracking underneath all of it. If the feed is why Shopping is starving, that is yours. If the page is why the clicks do not convert, that is yours too. Our team ships advertorials, comparison pages, and PDPs in Claude Code, deploys them to Vercel, points a subdomain at them, and tests them live before anything touches the client's Shopify theme.

You are expected to have an opinion about attribution and to defend it. We optimize to NC-CPA and NC-ROAS, not blended and not last click. We have turned brand search off to see what actually shifts to organic. We run geo holdouts. If a campaign is not incremental, we would rather know than keep the number.

You can live anywhere. We are remote and we hire worldwide. The one hard requirement is that you can take client calls during US Eastern business hours, because you are the client's point of contact. The rest of your day is yours. Nobody here is on a time clock. We judge you on output.

If you want a lane, a ticket queue, and a scope document, this is a bad fit and we will both know it fast.

If you want to own the whole picture and be judged on whether the number moved, keep reading.

Requirements

What the job looks like


Own a set of DTC accounts as the strategist, the buyer, and the client's direct point of contact. Budgets run from $5k/mo to well into six figures a month

description:
Everyone can run a search campaign. Almost nobody can tell you whether it worked.

That is the whole job.

Google will happily show you a 6x ROAS built almost entirely out of people who already knew your client's name. It will auto apply assets you did not ask for. It will report a number that makes a client feel great and tells you nothing about whether you grew the business.

So we do not hire people to manage Google Ads. We hire marketers who can tell the difference between demand they created and demand they harvested, and who can prove it to a client's face.

At Sweat Pants Agency we work with around 50 DTC and eCommerce brands, 20 to 25 of them on paid media. We spend $6 to $9M a month on Meta and $1 to $2M a month on Google. We are the only agency behind two INC #1 fastest growing brands, both from zero.

You would own a set of our Google accounts end to end.

Here is what "end to end" actually means.

You are the account manager. We do not have any. You talk to the client directly. You write the updates, you run the calls, and you defend the call you made. The reason we do it this way is ownership. When you are the person answering for the account, it is your result, not somebody else's summary of your result.

You own the whole funnel, not the campaign. Feed and Merchant Center, search and Shopping and PMax, Demand Gen and YouTube, the landing page, and the conversion tracking underneath all of it. If the feed is why Shopping is starving, that is yours. If the page is why the clicks do not convert, that is yours too. Our team ships advertorials, comparison pages, and PDPs in Claude Code, deploys them to Vercel, points a subdomain at them, and tests them live before anything touches the client's Shopify theme.

You are expected to have an opinion about attribution and to defend it. We optimize to NC-CPA and NC-ROAS, not blended and not last click. We have turned brand search off to see what actually shifts to organic. We run geo holdouts. If a campaign is not incremental, we would rather know than keep the number.

You can live anywhere. We are remote and we hire worldwide. The one hard requirement is that you can take client calls during US Eastern business hours, because you are the client's point of contact. The rest of your day is yours. Nobody here is on a time clock. We judge you on output.

If you want a lane, a ticket queue, and a scope document, this is a bad fit and we will both know it fast.

This role has been designated as ‘Remote/Teleworker’, which means you will primarily work from home.

Who We Are

Hewlett Packard Enterprise is the global edge-to-cloud company advancing the way people live and work. We help companies connect, protect, analyze, and act on their data and applications wherever they live, from edge to cloud, so they can turn insights into outcomes at the speed required to thrive in today’s complex world. Our culture thrives on finding new and better ways to accelerate what’s next. We know varied backgrounds are valued and succeed here. We have the flexibility to manage our work and personal needs. We make bold moves, together, and are a force for good. If you are looking to stretch and grow your career our culture will embrace you. Open up opportunities with HPE.

Job Description

The Product Adoption Content and Education (PACE) team develops and delivers the content our customers need to install, manage, and configure HPE Networking’s products and solutions. HPE Networking is all about powering connections and empowering change.

We are looking for an HPE Aruba Networking Courseware Developer to join our mighty team! In this role you’ll create customer-focused content, including comprehensive concepts, examples, tasks, reference information, and in-product guidance for HPE Networking’s cutting-edge cloud services, automation, and Network Management products. You’ll also have opportunities to lead technical documentation projects. The role requires the ability to grasp and translate complex technologies into easy-to-use content for our customers.

The ideal candidate is a subject matter expert in the content, and a persistent self-starter with strong collaborative skills who also has an interest in leading technical documentation projects. This ideal candidate enjoys continuous learning and professional growth and can excel in a fast-paced, highly-technical working environment. 

Responsibilities


Design, develop, deliver, and maintain customer-facing, best-in-class user content.
Produce a range of deliverables, including concepts and tasks for networking features, in-product content, installation instructions, illustrations, video scripts, course modules, and more.
Collaborate with key stakeholders and subject matter experts to understand and identify requirements and customer needs.
Analyze specifications and product descriptions and recommend the best learning approach.
Learn the customer experience through hands-on usage of our networking products.
Follow established style and process guidelines to provide consistency and completeness.


Minimum Qualifications


Demonstrated ability to produce high-quality, accurate, and easy-to-use technical content, preferably for advanced software products.
5+ years of experience producing technical content. 
BA/BS in Technical Writing, English, Computer Science, or related degree/networking certification or comparable experience.
Good understanding of technology concepts such as cloud computing, automation, networking, data centers, security, or other advanced software technology.
Ability to research complex technical concepts (independently and collaboratively). 
Familiarity with XML authoring, content management, and courseware development tools.
Strong problem-solving skills; ability to make progress with less-than-complete information.
Excellent communication and collaboration skills.
Ability to utilize AI tools to scale the creation of content, retaining high quality output.


Preferred Qualifications


Hands-on experience with network technologies, including routing, switching, security, network automation, virtual machines, containers, and cloud-services.
Hands-on experience with networking technologies such as cloud networking, routing, switching, data centers, or network security.
Familiarity with DITA/XML authoring principles and content management concepts.
Familiarity with Markdown and MS PowerPoint for authoring content.
Familiarity with program management methodologies and systems such as Agile and JIRA.
Familiarity with the HPE Aruba Networking and/or HPE Juniper Networking products and technologies.
Have industry network certifications.

description:
Misión del rol




Eres el dueño único de la relación con el cliente después del cierre comercial: respondes por que la cuenta obtenga valor medible de la plataforma, por su retención y por el crecimiento de su revenue. Orquestas el ciclo completo — handoff, implementación, go-live, estabilización y expansión — sin autoridad formal sobre Deployment, Producto o Soporte, consiguiendo que entreguen a través de relación e influencia, no de jerarquía.




En este rol vas a trabajar en:




1. Handoff y Arranque de Cuenta


Recibir el handoff formal del Sales Owner en una sesión dedicada: qué se vendió, qué se prometió, quién decide, quién usa, quién paga y qué espera el cliente



Validar que el modelo de cobro quedó explícito, incluido qué se factura por consumo y a qué tarifa



Recibir y cuestionar el Statement of Work, levantando lo que falte antes de arrancar



Mapear a los stakeholders del cliente (contraparte técnica, funcional y decisora) y registrar la cuenta en HubSpot desde el día uno



Conducir la sesión consultiva que levanta el alcance funcional del SOW, defenderlo ante el cliente y cerrar su firma




2. Ejecución y Orquestación del Proyecto


Liderar el weekly de avance con el cliente y mantener vivo el plan: dependencias, responsables, fechas y riesgos



Hacer push sobre el cliente para destrabar lo que impide avanzar (aprobaciones internas, accesos, documentación pendiente)



Escalar internamente a tiempo lo que no avanza, con contexto y con una propuesta, no solo con el problema



Levantar los controles de cambio, dimensionarlos con Deployment y cotizarlos antes de que se ejecuten



Registrar la gestión en ClickUp, con trazabilidad de bloqueos y de su causa




3. Go-Live, Estabilización y Adopción


Acompañar el día del lanzamiento, recorrer el checklist de salida con Deployment y cerrar el acta de entrega



Dar la capacitación de entrega al cliente: uso de la plataforma, módulos y lectura de métricas



Monitorear el consumo y la salud de los agentes (activos contra dormidos, volumen, casos de uso en producción contra los contratados) y mantener el health score actualizado



Revisar conversaciones reales para detectar dónde el flujo no responde, y cerrar brechas de adopción (módulos sin usar, usuarios sin capacitar)




4. Desarrollo de Cuenta y Renovación


Crecer lo ya vendido (volumen, nuevos casos de uso, canales, unidades de negocio) y vender lo que el cliente no tiene, con discovery y estimación junto a Deployment



Analizar la cuenta desde la data para encontrar la oportunidad antes de que el cliente la pida



Construir el caso de negocio y registrar la oportunidad en HubSpot con origen y monto estimado



Ejecutar business reviews recurrentes y ser dueño del proceso de renovación de punta a punta




5. Voz del Cliente


Agregar y priorizar el feedback del cliente en solicitudes accionables de producto



Documentar patrones de éxito, playbooks y casos que eleven el nivel de todo el equipo



Colaborar con Marketing en customer stories y referencias



Este rol es para ti si:

Tienes 3 o más años de experiencia en Customer Success, Account Management o roles client-facing en B2B SaaS o servicios tecnológicos



Tienes track record verificable manejando renovaciones, reduciendo churn y generando revenue de expansión sobre una cartera propia



Has coordinado proyectos y equipos que no te reportan — planes, dependencias, fechas y riesgos — y puedes dar un ejemplo de haber detectado una desviación antes de que fuera evidente



Has liderado sesiones de levantamiento de requerimientos con cliente y traducido lo que dice en un alcance documentado



Manejas un CRM y un gestor de proyectos (HubSpot y ClickUp o equivalentes)



Sabes leer y analizar datos de uso para construir un business review con información de varias fuentes



Español nativo e inglés profesional escrito y hablado (portugués suma como plus adicional)




Plus (deseable, no eliminatorio):


Experiencia en IA conversacional, plataformas de chatbots o tecnología de contact center



Curiosidad técnica: ha configurado integraciones, escrito llamadas básicas de API o trabajado de cerca con equipos de ingeniería



Familiaridad con el mercado enterprise de LATAM (servicios financieros, telecom, retail, salud)



Experiencia con modelos de pricing por consumo



Qué buscamos en esta persona

Visión de negocio: puede explicar cómo gana dinero un cliente típico y conectar ese modelo con un caso de uso concreto de la plataforma, sin que se lo pidan dos veces



Influencia sin autoridad: tiene un ejemplo verificable de haber conseguido que un equipo que no le reporta (Deployment, Producto, Ingeniería) entregara a tiempo, construyendo relación en vez de escalar



Organización bajo presión: sostiene varias cuentas y frentes simultáneos sin perder trazabilidad — documenta bloqueos, causas y siguientes pasos en la herramienta, no en su cabeza



Ownership proactivo: detecta una señal de riesgo (health score, uso, sentiment) y actúa antes de que el cliente lo reclame o el problema escale, en vez de esperar instrucción



Pensamiento consultivo: cuestiona un requerimiento del cliente cuando hay una forma mejor de resolverlo, en vez de tomarlo al pie de la letra



Impacto esperado

Gross Revenue Retention (GRR) de la cartera asignada — por encima de 90%



Time-to-value en cuentas nuevas — menos de 30 días desde el arranque — por cuenta nueva

A fast-growing US healthcare technology company offering direct-to-consumer and B2B laboratory testing is looking for an Operations Coordinator to deliver highly responsive customer support, document scalable processes, and build AI-powered workflows that reduce manual work.

Its support operation already deflects about 70% of cases through AI, and the team is pushing that number higher.

Day-to-day, you will work in Slack, Intercom, and Notion, splitting your time across customer support (about 40%), process documentation (30%), AI automation (25%), and B2B partner operations (5%). This is a Wednesday to Sunday role, so you will keep operations moving through the weekend when the rest of the team is offline. Success means fast and consistent response times, documentation others can follow without help, and a measurable increase in case deflection and automation rates within your first 90 days.

Customer Support & Communication

Build new processes to support multiple concurrent client implementations

Keep the knowledge base current as products, partners, and policies change

AI Automation & Workflow Optimization

Build and refine Intercom Fin workflows to raise case deflection above the current 70%

Identify manual tasks outside Intercom and build AI-powered workflows to remove them

Connect automations across Intercom, Slack, and Notion

B2B Partner Operations

Track partner requests and implementation tasks through to completion

Log all partner communication so handoffs stay clean

Must-Have

2+ years in customer support operations, customer operations, or operations coordination, with at least 1 year at a startup or scale-up

Direct customer-facing support experience handling B2C or B2B inquiries through chat, email, or ticketing channels

Hands-on Intercom experience (inbox, help center, macros, or workflows)

Built at least one automated support or operations workflow (Intercom Fin, Zendesk AI, Zapier, Make, or equivalent) with a measurable result such as case deflection rate, automation rate, or hours saved

Created SOPs, process documentation, or knowledge base articles from scratch in Notion or an equivalent wiki, with daily Slack use

Available 9:00 AM – 6:00 PM PST, Wednesday – Sunday, including full Saturday and Sunday shifts

C1+ English (CEFR) for direct communication with US customers and lab partners

Nice-to-Have

Intercom Fin AI Agent configuration, including agentic procedures or multi-step workflows

Healthcare, laboratory testing, telehealth, or digital health operations experience

Working knowledge of HIPAA-compliant handling of patient data

Experience supporting both B2C customers and B2B partners in the same role, including partner logistics or implementation coordination

El equipo de operaciones de External Fulfillment UAF se divide en dos roles complementarios:

Field Support Team (FST): Equipo de soporte en piso responsable de alinear las operaciones a través de auditorías físicas, visitando almacenes de vendedores según se requiera.

Flow Support Team: Equipo que maneja operaciones mediante el monitoreo diario y conversaciones remotas con los proveedores, dando seguimiento a casos específicos y garantizando el cumplimiento de estándares operativos.

Tu Rol

Como Flow Support Specialist, serás el puente entre Amazon y nuestros socios comerciales, monitoreando indicadores clave y procesos estándar para ayudar a los vendedores externos a tener una experiencia sin dificultades al vender en Amazon. Identificarás errores operativos, preverás implicaciones basadas en datos, y trabajarás en la mejora continua de nuestras operaciones.

Key job responsibilities

Responsabilidades Clave


 Monitorear el desempeño de una variedad de sitios asignados, enfocándose en métricas críticas como on-time shipment
 Analizar datos de distintas fuentes, identificar información relevante y presentarla de manera clara para la toma de decisiones
 Prever implicaciones operativas basadas en el análisis de datos y sus tendencias
 Ser el punto de contacto entre clientes internos y externos, manteniendo los objetivos y límites de comunicación de acuerdo con la privacidad de información
 Entrenar y dirigir a las distintas operaciones de los vendedores para tomar acción y cumplir con las normas establecidas
 Identificar causas raíz de problemáticas operativas y ayudar a los proveedores a prevenir y controlar las situaciones detectadas
 Crear y dar seguimiento a indicadores operativos, generando propuestas para nuevas metodologías de automatización
 Notificar y actualizar de manera organizada y precisa cualquier situación relevante, direccionando escalaciones cuando sea necesario
 Proponer e implementar mejoras continuas en los procesos operativos

 Experience with Excel
 High school diploma or equivalent


Preferred Qualifications


 Experience with SQL
 Experience in data collection and ability to draft clear and detailed requirements documents

description:
About Influur

Influur is reimagining how advertising works through creators, data, and AI. Our mission is to make influencer marketing as measurable, predictable, and scalable as paid media, and we’re building the tech that makes it possible.

Backed by top-tier investors and trusted by global brands, we’re scaling fast across music, culture, and entertainment.

We’re looking for a

List Builder

who’s excited to discover the right creators for every campaign, turning brand briefs into highly relevant, strategic creator lists. You’ll combine research, data, cultural awareness, and strong judgment to identify creators who truly fit each brand, audience, and campaign objective.

Your Skillset

Must-haves

1+ years of experience

in influencer marketing, creator marketing, talent sourcing, social media, digital marketing, or a similar role.

Hands-on experience

researching, sourcing, and evaluating creators

across platforms such as TikTok, Instagram, and YouTube.

Strong understanding of

creator and brand fit , including audience demographics, engagement, content style, market relevance, and brand alignment.

Ability to translate a

campaign or client brief into clear creator selection criteria

and build targeted lists accordingly.

Strong knowledge of

social media trends, creators, digital culture, and emerging communities .

Ability to work with

high volumes of creator profiles and multiple briefs simultaneously

while maintaining accuracy and quality.

Strong research skills and attention to detail, with the ability to go beyond obvious or repetitive creator choices.

Comfortable working with

data and performance metrics

to support creator recommendations.

Strong organizational skills and ability to work quickly in a fast-paced environment with changing priorities.

Professional proficiency in

English and Spanish .

Nice-to-haves

Experience working at an

influencer marketing agency, creator platform, talent agency, or fast-growing startup .

Experience sourcing creators for campaigns in

music, beauty, entertainment, CPG, or lifestyle .

Familiarity with influencer marketing platforms, social listening tools, or creator discovery tools.

Experience using

AI tools to accelerate creator research, analyze profiles, identify trends, or improve sourcing workflows .

Experience supporting campaigns across multiple markets, particularly the

US and LATAM .

You’re The Type Who

Has an eye for creators.

You can look at a brief and quickly understand what kind of creator makes sense, beyond follower count alone.

Is naturally curious.

You enjoy going down the rabbit hole of TikTok, Instagram, YouTube, trends, communities, and emerging creators to find profiles others might miss.

Moves fast without sacrificing quality.

You understand that creator marketing moves quickly and can deliver strong lists under tight timelines.

Thinks beyond the obvious.

You don’t rely on the same creators everyone already knows. You’re resourceful and creative in how you search.

Is highly organized and detail-oriented.

You can manage hundreds of profiles, multiple briefs, and changing requirements without losing track of the details.

Takes ownership.

If a list isn’t strong enough, you don’t wait for someone to tell you. You keep searching, refining, and improving it.

Is AI-curious.

You’re excited to experiment with AI and automation to research faster, identify better matches, and improve the way creator sourcing gets done.

Thrives in startup environments.

You’re comfortable with speed, ambiguity, changing priorities, and figuring things out as you go.

Cares about the “why.”

You don’t just add a creator because they meet a checklist. You can explain why they’re a strong fit for the campaign.

What we offer

Competitive equity in a venture-backed company.

Opportunities to grow fast and develop.

Remote work.

Direct connection to our exclusive community of influencers — from global stars to the next big thing.

skills: Own a set of DTC accounts as the strategist, the buyer, and the client's direct point of contact. Budgets run from $5k/mo to well into six figures a month
Own the client relationship. There is no account manager between you and them. You present the results, the plan, and the reasoning, and you are the one who answers when something is not working

Audit before you touch anything. Every account we take over gets a real review first: campaign and ad group structure, keywords versus search terms, negatives, bidding strategy per campaign type, impression share, feed health, landing pages, audiences, and conversion tracking. Then a Loom walking the client through what you found. That Loom is how we sell and it is how we keep people

Run brand and non brand as different businesses. Brand is mostly assisted conversion and it usually belongs on target impression share, not target CPA. Non brand is where the growth is and where the waste is. Report them separately or you are reporting nothing

Know what PMax is actually doing. The most common mistake we see is optimizing PMax against an incremental CAC when half the volume inside it is branded. If you cannot separate those two, you cannot set a target
Keep Google's automation on a leash. Auto applied recommendations, auto applied assets, and auto created sitelinks have cost our clients real money. We audit for them on a schedule
Own the feed. Merchant Center hygiene, product titles, disapprovals, promotions, and what the feed does to Shopping and PMax delivery

Own the tracking. GA4, GTM, Shopify goal imports versus a raw Google Ads tag, enhanced conversions, offline conversion imports for the lead gen accounts. When the numbers do not reconcile, you are the one who finds out why
Diagnose the bottleneck, then go fix it. Creative, offer, AOV, landing page, checkout, tracking. Nobody is going to reassign it to another team
Build the things the account needs. Landing pages, scripts, reporting, whatever removes the constraint. We are heavy AI users and we expect you to build, not just prompt

You have done this with real money. Hands on Google Ads at meaningful spend on DTC and eCommerce, with results you can walk us through: CPA, ROAS, revenue, and what you actually changed to get them. Shopping and PMax specifically, not just search
You are fluent in the whole stack, not one campaign type. Search, Shopping, PMax, Demand Gen, YouTube, Merchant Center, GA4, GTM. Bing is a nice to have

You are AI native, and you build. This is a requirement, not a bonus. You should already be using Claude or equivalent as a working tool rather than a novelty, and you should be able to build and ship a landing page with it

You can communicate your ideas in English at a native or near native level. You will be in front of clients constantly. You need to explain your thinking clearly, sell an idea on its merits, push back when a client is about to force the account into mediocrity, and raise a problem before it becomes a fire. This matters as much as anything else on this list
You are skeptical of your own numbers. You would rather run the holdout than protect the dashboard
You can work US Eastern business hours for client calls. Where you live is up to you
Bonus: you have built or operated your own Shopify store, or you have run Meta at spend too
"That was not my role" is in your vocabulary. It is the fastest way to end an interview here. If the feed was the problem on an account you ran, you should have done something about the feed
You want to be told what to do this week
You need a ticketing system to know what matters
You quote blended ROAS as if it settles the question
description:
Everyone can run a search campaign. Almost nobody can tell you whether it worked.

That is the whole job.

Google will happily show you a 6x ROAS built almost entirely out of people who already knew your client's name. It will auto apply assets you did not ask for. It will report a number that makes a client feel great and tells you nothing about whether you grew the business.

So we do not hire people to manage Google Ads. We hire marketers who can tell the difference between demand they created and demand they harvested, and who can prove it to a client's face.

At Sweat Pants Agency we work with around 50 DTC and eCommerce brands, 20 to 25 of them on paid media. We spend $6 to $9M a month on Meta and $1 to $2M a month on Google. We are the only agency behind two INC #1 fastest growing brands, both from zero.

You would own a set of our Google accounts end to end.

Here is what "end to end" actually means.

You are the account manager. We do not have any. You talk to the client directly. You write the updates, you run the calls, and you defend the call you made. The reason we do it this way is ownership. When you are the person answering for the account, it is your result, not somebody else's summary of your result.

You own the whole funnel, not the campaign. Feed and Merchant Center, search and Shopping and PMax, Demand Gen and YouTube, the landing page, and the conversion tracking underneath all of it. If the feed is why Shopping is starving, that is yours. If the page is why the clicks do not convert, that is yours too. Our team ships advertorials, comparison pages, and PDPs in Claude Code, deploys them to Vercel, points a subdomain at them, and tests them live before anything touches the client's Shopify theme.

You are expected to have an opinion about attribution and to defend it. We optimize to NC-CPA and NC-ROAS, not blended and not last click. We have turned brand search off to see what actually shifts to organic. We run geo holdouts. If a campaign is not incremental, we would rather know than keep the number.

You can live anywhere. We are remote and we hire worldwide. The one hard requirement is that you can take client calls during US Eastern business hours, because you are the client's point of contact. The rest of your day is yours. Nobody here is on a time clock. We judge you on output.

At Sweat Pants Agency we work with around 50 DTC and eCommerce brands, 20 to 25 of them on paid media. We spend $6 to $9M a month on Meta and $1 to $2M a month on Google. We are the only agency behind two INC #1 fastest growing brands, both from zero.

Everyone can run a search campaign. Almost nobody can tell you whether it worked.

That is the whole job.

Google will happily show you a 6x ROAS built almost entirely out of people who already knew your client's name. It will auto apply assets you did not ask for. It will report a number that makes a client feel great and tells you nothing about whether you grew the business.

So we do not hire people to manage Google Ads. We hire marketers who can tell the difference between demand they created and demand they harvested, and who can prove it to a client's face.

At Sweat Pants Agency we work with around 50 DTC and eCommerce brands, 20 to 25 of them on paid media. We spend $6 to $9M a month on Meta and $1 to $2M a month on Google. We are the only agency behind two INC #1 fastest growing brands, both from zero.

You would own a set of our Google accounts end to end.

Here is what "end to end" actually means.

You are the account manager. We do not have any. You talk to the client directly. You write the updates, you run the calls, and you defend the call you made. The reason we do it this way is ownership. When you are the person answering for the account, it is your result, not somebody else's summary of your result.

You own the whole funnel, not the campaign. Feed and Merchant Center, search and Shopping and PMax, Demand Gen and YouTube, the landing page, and the conversion tracking underneath all of it. You are expected to have an opinion about attribution and to defend it. We optimize to NC-CPA and NC-ROAS, not blended and not last click. You can live anywhere. We are remote and we hire worldwide. The one hard requirement is that you can take client calls during US Eastern business hours, because you are the client's point of contact. The rest of your day is yours. Nobody here is on a time clock. We judge you on output.

skills: Proficiency in spoken and written English at an advanced level is required for this role.

Own the MMM data layer in Snowflake. Build and maintain model-ready daily and weekly marts for each client that combine paid media (spend, impressions, clicks by channel and campaign), ecommerce revenue and orders (new vs. returning, gross and net, refunds, discounts), site and email/SMS data from GA4, and any non-media drivers. Every mart has consistent channel groupings, currencies and timezones.

Own the MMT geo data layer. Build geo-level media and sales tables at DMA (or Comscore), state and zip level for every major platform (Meta, Google, TikTok, Pinterest, Amazon, Microsoft, Programmatic, etc.) and for CMS/CRM/Amazon/Retail Datsets, with standard market names that line up across sources. These tables feed automated market selection, pre-period validation, synthetic control models and test readouts.

Build and automate a data quality process. Turn the checks we currently run manually into automated Snowflake/dbt tests and alerts: date gaps, zero-spend or zero-revenue days, cost without impressions (and the reverse), duplicated or unmatched markets, outlier spikes, restatement drift and source freshness. Problems should be flagged before a model is trained or a test is read out.
Own and maintain model logs and exported model outputs (contributions, response curves, adstock, optimization results) well structured, versioned and easy to query.
Support onboarding of new measurement clients. Own and maintain a repeatable, mostly automated process: map their data feeds, check history depth and quality, and flag gaps before modeling starts.

Handle client-specific data needs as they come up. You are not responsible for client workflow, but you may need to jump in to assist the team as things come up.. Write client-specific overrides, channel mappings and marts when a client needs them, and decide whether each piece of logic belongs in the shared core or in the client's own layer.
Use AI coding tools to work faster (Claude Code, Cursor, Copilot, Hex's AI agent), and document the patterns that work so the team adopts them.
3+ years in data or analytics engineering, including 1+ year owning a production dbt project of meaningful size.
Advanced SQL and Python, with production-grade pipeline code.
Deep dbt expertise: incremental models vs. full refreshes, Jinja and macros, tests, snapshots, source freshness, exposures, and keeping a large DAG under control.
Strong Snowflake skills: semi-structured/VARIANT data, dynamic per-client queries, query and cost tuning, permissions across separate client databases.
Hands-on marketing and ecommerce data experience: ad-platform APIs, UTMs, attribution windows, platform-reported vs. warehouse-reported conversions, Shopify order and refund logic.

An understanding of what measurement models need from data: a continuous time series, consistent granularity, stable channel definitions, enough history, and the reasons one bad week or market can skew results.
Experience building multi-client data models, with the judgment to know when logic belongs in the shared core and when it belongs in a client layer.
Git and CI/CD with automated testing you trust.
Real adoption of AI-assisted development workflows.
Comfort shipping iteratively based on feedback from analysts and app users.
Direct MMM or incrementality experience (Meridian, Robyn, PyMC-Marketing, synthetic control/causal impact, geo-lift).
Experience with geographic data: DMA/zip mappings, population and market-size data.

description:
We are looking for a Consumer Experience (CX) Regional Manager to join a key Emerging Markets Business Unit within Kraft Heinz International. In this role, you will serve as the primary CX partner to the regional R&D, Marketing and Commercial teams, ensuring product and pack decisions are grounded in deep consumer understanding and aligned with business priorities.

You will lead the regional Consumer Experience agenda across Product & Pack Superiority, Design to Value and Innovation programs, translating integrated consumer, sensory and category learning into actionable recommendations that drive business growth and portfolio competitiveness.

As part of the broader Consumer & Culinary Experience network, you will collaborate closely with global and central CX teams to deploy best practices, leverage global learning and ensure alignment of methodologies and ways of working across regions. In addition, you will lead the regional sensory capability through management of sensory resources and strategic partnerships, ensuring high-quality sensory learning and strong alignment with global standards and best practices.

Responsibilities


Lead Product & Pack Superiority programs across the region, identifying performance gaps and recommending actions to improve consumer experience, product performance and business results.
Drive Portfolio Healthiness and Design to Value initiatives by integrating consumer desirability into value engineering, reformulation, and recipe & pack design decisions.
Translate consumer growth opportunities into product and pack innovation strategies through integrated consumer, sensory and category insights.
Define and execute consumer and sensory learning plans, leveraging internal and external capabilities to support key business decisions.
Lead regional sensory capability, managing sensory resources, external partnerships and deployment of sensory best practices aligned with global standards.


Key Accountabilities


Own the regional CX roadmap aligned to Business Unit priorities.
Deliver impactful Product & Pack Superiority programs that improve portfolio competitiveness.
Support successful deployment of Cost Value initiatives while protecting consumer experience and brand equity.
Build a pipeline of consumer-led product and pack innovation opportunities.
Deliver high-quality and meaningful consumer and sensory insights that enables confident business decisions.
Ensure strong regional sensory capabilities and alignment with global standards and partners.
Strengthen Voice of Consumer activation and consumer-centric decision making across the Business Unit.


Qualifications And Education Requirements


University degree (Master's or PhD) in Consumer Science, Sensory Science, Psychology, Behavioral Science, Marketing Research, Food Science or related field.
8+ years of experience in Consumer Experience, Consumer Insights, Sensory Science or Innovation Research.
Strong expertise in quantitative and qualitative consumer research methodologies.
Strong understanding of sensory science methodologies and product experience evaluation.
Experience supporting innovation, superiority, renovation and portfolio improvement programs in corporate environment.
English level advanced or fluent.

description:
RUDOLF MÉXICO forma parte del GRUPO RUDOLF, una empresa con presencia mundial y líder tecnológico en productos químicos especializados innovadores para la construcción, los recubrimientos y las aplicaciones textiles. Gracias a nuestra fuerte capacidad de I+D, una red de producción mundial y un compromiso constante con la sostenibilidad, ofrecemos soluciones de alto rendimiento para pinturas, recubrimientos, aplanados y materiales de construcción.




Para apoyar la expansión de nuestro negocio de Construcción y Recubrimientos en México, buscamos un/a Gerente/a de Desarrollo Comercial con espíritu emprendedor que lidere el desarrollo del mercado de nuestra cartera de Productos Químicos para la Construcción y Aditivos para Recubrimientos, establezca relaciones estratégicas con los clientes e impulse un crecimiento empresarial sostenible.

title: Revenue Operations Analyst
skills: Build and maintain Tableau dashboards tracking performance across our partnerships channel and new growth initiatives — serving audiences from country leads to executive leadership.
Analyze conversion rates, pipeline health, ramp trends, and revenue attainment across programs and segments, surfacing patterns before they become decisions that have already been made.
Come with a point of view. When a program is underperforming or a trend shifts, bring an interpretation and a recommendation (not just a chart).
Support quarterly and annual GTM business reviews with structured analysis: cohort breakdowns, market-level benchmarks, and forward-looking indicators.
Contribute to GTM capacity planning and quota-setting cycles — modeling scenarios, building attainment reports, and stress-testing assumptions before plans are finalized.
Maintain performance-against-target reporting for growth programs and emerging channels: track attainment, flag outliers early, and ensure data is always reconciled.
Support variable compensation analysis for relevant programs — running calculations, auditing for accuracy, and partnering with Finance to ensure payouts are correct and timely.
Build and maintain data structures that support reliable rolling forecasts for new and high-growth segments.

Use AI tools, including Claude and other frontier models, as active parts of your workflow: automating repetitive reporting tasks, accelerating data synthesis, and building scalable analytical programs that would otherwise require a much larger team.
Identify RevOps processes that can be operationalized or significantly improved through AI, and take ownership of building those solutions, not just flagging the opportunity.
Apply AI-assisted analysis to extract insights at scale from large, multi-source datasets: pipeline signals, rep activity, customer behavior, and market trends.
Help establish Jeeves’s AI-first approach to RevOps as a model for how the broader GTM team operates.
Share responsibility for data quality across our revenue stack (HubSpot CRM, Tableau, and financial systems), conducting audits for accuracy, completeness, and consistency.
Connect disparate data sources (CRM, marketing automation, financial tools, and proprietary revenue data) so that reporting on growth programs is unified and trustworthy.
Document data models, metric definitions, and reporting logic so the team works from a shared understanding of what we’re measuring and why.
Develop enough context on our GTM motion to contribute meaningfully in planning and pipeline review cycles alongside sales leadership, bringing data that drives decisions, not just awareness.
Serve as a reliable analytical resource to the Head of Revenue Operations and GTM leadership: scope requests clearly, pull the data, and return clear answers quickly.
Identify process gaps and proactively propose improvements to how we collect, manage, and act on GTM data (especially across new and growing channels).
Tableau mastery: able to write complex calculated fields, build multi-source dashboards, and design views for diverse audiences from reps to the C-suite.
Advanced Excel and Google Sheets: complex formulas, pivot tables, and financial modeling — you reach for the right tool for the job, not just the most impressive one.
Strong SQL skills: you can get to an answer independently without waiting for a data engineer to pull it for you.
Data integration experience: comfortable connecting CRM, marketing automation, and financial data into unified reporting environments.
Business metrics fluency: deep understanding of conversion rates, customer lifetime value (LTV), pipeline coverage, ramp curves, revenue attainment, and customer health.
Data modeling: able to design clean structures that support accurate forecasting, compensation analysis, and multi-region rollups.
You actively use AI tools, Claude Copilot/Code, or equivalent, as part of your day-to-day workflow, not as a novelty.
You’ve used AI to automate reporting pipelines, accelerate analysis, or build operational programs that scale beyond what a single analyst could do manually.
You’re curious about where AI can go next in RevOps and you bring ideas, not just execution.
Hungry and driven: you want to build something generational, and you bring the energy and output to match. You hold yourself to a higher standard than anyone else will hold you to.
Thrives in high-velocity environments: you’re not just comfortable with ambiguity and shifting priorities — you’re energized by them. You find a way through, not a reason to wait.

description:
Jeeves is the stablecoin-native banking platform for global enterprises. Thousands of companies across 35 countries run their corporate cards, payments, treasury and spend on one platform, with more than $5B in annualized volume, payouts to 190 countries, and one of the fastest-growing stablecoin payment networks in the world. BMW, H&M, Lululemon, Burger King, Kavak and XP are among them, and more than 80% of customers use multiple Jeeves products.

We chose hard problems on purpose.

We hire for one thing: relentlessness. A strong motor that keeps going when the problem has no playbook. You'll know in your first week if Jeeves is right for you. For the right people, it's the steepest learning curve of your career.

Jeeves has raised more than $400 million in equity funding from Andreessen Horowitz, Y Combinator, CRV, Coinbase Ventures, GIC, AllianceBernstein, CoinFund and others.

If you want to rebuild how money moves across borders, come build it with us.

This role is focused on Jeeves’s growth programs and emerging revenue channels — including our partnerships channel and new market expansion initiatives — where we need rigorous, scalable analytics to match the pace of growth.

You’ll be responsible for the analytical layer that connects our sales activity to revenue outcomes: building the dashboards our leadership relies on, maintaining shared responsibility for the integrity of our performance data, and proactively surfacing the insights that shape how we operate. You’ll work closely with the Head of Revenue Operations and contribute meaningfully to planning and review cycles alongside GTM leadership.

The pace here is real. Priorities shift, timelines compress, and the ground moves under your feet — not occasionally, but constantly. We need someone who is energized by that, not worn down. You won’t wait for someone to tell you what to look at. You’ll already know.

Key Responsibilities

 GTM Analytics & Growth Program Insights 


 Build and maintain Tableau dashboards tracking performance across our partnerships channel and new growth initiatives — serving audiences from country leads to executive leadership. 
 Analyze conversion rates, pipeline health, ramp trends, and revenue attainment across programs and segments, surfacing patterns before they become decisions that have already been made. 
 Come with a point of view. When a program is underperforming or a trend shifts, bring an interpretation and a recommendation (not just a chart). 
 Support quarterly and annual GTM business reviews with structured analysis: cohort breakdowns, market-level benchmarks, and forward-looking indicators. 


 Revenue Planning & Target Analysis 


 Contribute to GTM capacity planning and quota-setting cycles — modeling scenarios, building attainment reports, and stress-testing assumptions before plans are finalized. 
 Maintain performance-against-target reporting for growth programs and emerging channels: track attainment, flag outliers early, and ensure data is always reconciled. 
 Support variable compensation analysis for relevant programs — running calculations, auditing for accuracy, and partnering with Finance to ensure payouts are correct and timely. 
 Build and maintain data structures that support reliable rolling forecasts for new and high-growth segments. 


 AI-Driven Operations & Scale 


 Use AI tools, including Claude and other frontier models, as active parts of your workflow: automating repetitive reporting tasks, accelerating data synthesis, and building scalable analytical programs that would otherwise require a much larger team. 
 Identify RevOps processes that can be operationalized or significantly improved through AI, and take ownership of building those solutions, not just flagging the opportunity. 
 Apply AI-assisted analysis to extract insights at scale from large, multi-source datasets: pipeline signals, rep activity, customer behavior, and market trends. 
 Help establish Jeeves’s AI-first approach to RevOps as a model for how the broader GTM team operates. 


 Data Quality & Systems Integration 


 Share responsibility for data quality across our revenue stack (HubSpot CRM, Tableau, and financial systems), conducting audits for accuracy, completeness, and consistency. 
 Connect disparate data sources (CRM, marketing automation, financial tools, and proprietary revenue data) so that reporting on growth programs is unified and trustworthy. 
 Document data models, metric definitions, and reporting logic so the team works from a shared understanding of what we’re measuring and why. 


 Stakeholder Partnership 


 Develop enough context on our GTM motion to contribute meaningfully in planning and pipeline review cycles alongside sales leadership, bringing data that drives decisions, not just awareness. 
 Serve as a reliable analytical resource to the Head of Revenue Operations and GTM leadership: scope requests clearly, pull the data, and return clear answers quickly. 
 Identify process gaps and proactively propose improvements to how we collect, manage, and act on GTM data (especially across new and growing channels). 


What We’re Looking For

 Technical & Analytical Skills 


 Tableau mastery: able to write complex calculated fields, build multi-source dashboards, and design views for diverse audiences from reps to the C-suite. 
 Advanced Excel and Google Sheets: complex formulas, pivot tables, and financial modeling — you reach for the right tool for the job, not just the most impressive one. 
 Strong SQL skills: you can get to an answer independently without waiting for a data engineer to pull it for you. 
 Data integration experience: comfortable connecting CRM, marketing automation, and financial data into unified reporting environments. 
 Business metrics fluency: deep understanding of conversion rates, customer lifetime value (LTV), pipeline coverage, ramp curves, revenue attainment, and customer health. 
 Data modeling: able to design clean structures that support accurate forecasting, compensation analysis, and multi-region rollups. 


 AI Fluency (Required, Not Optional) 


 You actively use AI tools, Claude Copilot/Code, or equivalent, as part of your day-to-day workflow, not as a novelty. 
 You’ve used AI to automate reporting pipelines, accelerate analysis, or build operational programs that scale beyond what a single analyst could do manually. 
 You’re curious about where AI can go next in RevOps and you bring ideas, not just execution. 


 Soft Skills & Ways of Working 


 Hungry and driven: you want to build something generational, and you bring the energy and output to match. You hold yourself to a higher standard than anyone else will hold you to. 
 Thrives in high-velocity environments: you’re not just comfortable with ambiguity and shifting priorities — you’re energized by them. You find a way through, not a reason to wait.
